status: approved by the founder on 6 November 2026; chapters are written in order
notes: Depth standard (founder, 6 November 2026): every chapter climbs from its entry level to its ceiling, the hardest problems its topic produces, with a full problem ladder through the listed tiers (see course.json, depth_standard and tiers).
Prerequisites inside D06 use chapter IDs. Prerequisites in other domains are listed as text until those domains have ledgers.

Flags: mandatory-pilot-a/b/c and mandatory-quantum mark the chapters the master specification requires; expert-review marks chapters that need a qualified human reviewer before publication; bridge marks short catch-up lessons; history-needs-sources means every historical statement must be sourced.

groups.name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation

chapters.title: Why Complex Numbers Are Needed
chapters.objective: See exactly where the real numbers run out (x^2 + 1 = 0) and what it means to extend a number system consistently.
chapters.toughest: Cardano's formula on cubics with three real roots (Bombelli's example) and the casus irreducibilis; Frobenius's theorem: R, C and the quaternions are the only finite-dimensional associative real division algebras.
chapters.proofs: Proof that x^2 >= 0 for every real x.

chapters.title: Meeting i: Arithmetic with a + bi
chapters.objective: Add, subtract and multiply numbers of the form a + bi using i^2 = -1.
chapters.toughest: Powers like (1+i)^n and binomial sums via i; Gaussian integers, norms and which primes are sums of two squares.

chapters.title: Real and Imaginary Parts, and Equality
chapters.objective: Use Re and Im; solve equations by equating real and imaginary parts.
chapters.toughest: Equations mixing z, conj(z) and |z| (JEE Advanced style); functional equations over C.
chapters.proofs: Equality of complex numbers from the definition.

chapters.title: Complex Numbers as Ordered Pairs
chapters.objective: Build C as pairs (a, b) with defined addition and multiplication, and recover i as (0, 1).
chapters.toughest: Build C as R[x]/(x^2+1) and prove it isomorphic to the ordered-pair construction.

chapters.title: Checking the Field Laws
chapters.objective: Prove that the ordered-pair construction satisfies every field axiom.
chapters.toughest: Prove C is the unique degree-2 field extension of R up to isomorphism; why R^3 admits no field structure extending R (Frobenius context).
chapters.proofs: Complete proofs of commutativity, associativity, distributivity, identities and inverses.

chapters.title: The Conjugate and Its Rules
chapters.objective: Define the conjugate and prove its rules for sums and products.
chapters.toughest: Olympiad problems using z conj(z) = |z|^2; prove the only automorphisms of C fixing R are the identity and conjugation.

chapters.title: Division and Reciprocals
chapters.objective: Divide complex numbers by multiplying by the conjugate; find 1/z.
chapters.toughest: JEE Advanced and olympiad problems on rational expressions in z and conditions for real or purely imaginary quotients.
chapters.proofs: Derive the reciprocal formula and show it is the field inverse.

chapters.title: Why C Cannot Be Ordered
chapters.objective: Prove there is no ordering of C compatible with addition and multiplication.
chapters.toughest: Prove no field containing a square root of -1 can be ordered; Artin–Schreier: a field is orderable exactly when -1 is not a sum of squares.
chapters.proofs: Complete proof by contradiction using i.

chapters.title: R Inside C: A Consistent Extension
chapters.objective: Show the map a -> (a, 0) preserves the operations, so C genuinely extends R.
chapters.toughest: R is real closed and C = R(i) is algebraically closed; uniqueness of C up to isomorphism as an extension of R.
chapters.proofs: Embedding proof; R[x]/(x^2+1) remark marked advanced.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: The Complex Plane
chapters.objective: Picture complex numbers as points and arrows in the Argand plane.
chapters.toughest: JEE Advanced locus and region problems in the Argand plane.
chapters.lab: Plot points and read off Re and Im.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: Addition as Vector Addition
chapters.objective: See addition and subtraction as the parallelogram rule and displacement.
chapters.toughest: Olympiad vector geometry: centroids, parallelograms and concurrency via complex coordinates.
chapters.lab: Drag two points; watch the sum.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: Modulus: Distance from Zero
chapters.objective: Define |z| and prove |z|^2 = z times its conjugate.
chapters.toughest: Extremal problems for |z| under constraints (JEE Advanced and olympiad).
chapters.quantum: Probabilities are squared moduli of amplitudes.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: Properties of the Modulus
chapters.objective: Prove |zw| = |z||w| and |z/w| = |z|/|w|.
chapters.toughest: Modulus identities such as the parallelogram law and their olympiad applications.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: The Triangle Inequality
chapters.objective: Prove the triangle inequality, its equality cases and the reverse inequality.
chapters.toughest: Ptolemy's inequality and Hlawka's inequality via complex numbers; olympiad inequalities with equality cases.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: Distances, Circles and Regions
chapters.objective: Describe circles, discs and half-planes with equations in z.
chapters.toughest: Apollonius circles |z-a| = k|z-b|, regions and their intersections (JEE Advanced and olympiad).

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: Quadratic Equations with Complex Roots
chapters.objective: Solve any real quadratic over C; prove non-real roots of real polynomials come in conjugate pairs.
chapters.toughest: Location of roots, Vieta's relations and olympiad polynomial problems with complex roots.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: Square Roots of a Complex Number
chapters.objective: Find both square roots of a + bi algebraically.
chapters.toughest: Square roots of complex numbers inside harder equations and quadratic systems.
chapters.proofs: Derivation by equating parts; there are exactly two roots for nonzero z.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: Polynomials and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
chapters.objective: State the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra precisely and use it to factor polynomials.
chapters.toughest: Compare proofs of the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra (winding, Liouville, Galois); Gauss–Lucas theorem; bounds on root location.
chapters.proofs: Statement with hypotheses; proof deferred to C045.

chapters.group_name: Algebra and geometry of complex numbers
chapters.title: Geometry with Complex Numbers
chapters.objective: Use complex numbers for midpoints, rotation by i and similar triangles.
chapters.toughest: Olympiad geometry by complex coordinates: Napoleon's theorem, the nine-point circle, Simson lines.
chapters.proofs: Multiplication by i rotates by 90 degrees (algebraic proof).

chapters.title: Angles, Radians and the Unit Circle
chapters.objective: Bridge lesson: radians, sine and cosine on the unit circle.
chapters.toughest: Bridge: trigonometric identities and equations at JEE Advanced level.

chapters.title: Polar Form and the Argument
chapters.objective: Write z = r(cos t + i sin t); define arg and the principal value; avoid atan pitfalls.
chapters.toughest: Arguments of products and quotients, principal-value traps, arg-based loci (JEE Advanced).
chapters.proofs: Existence and uniqueness of polar form for nonzero z (argument up to 2 pi).

chapters.title: Multiplication Rotates and Scales
chapters.objective: Prove that moduli multiply and arguments add.
chapters.toughest: Olympiad geometry by rotation: equilateral and square constructions, spiral similarities.
chapters.proofs: Complete proof from the angle-addition formulas.
chapters.lab: Interactive rotation model: multiply by w and watch the plane turn and stretch.

chapters.title: De Moivre's Theorem
chapters.objective: Prove De Moivre's theorem for integer powers and derive trig identities.
chapters.toughest: Trigonometric sums and products via De Moivre; Chebyshev polynomials and their extremal property.
chapters.proofs: Proof by induction, including negative powers.

chapters.title: Roots of Unity and nth Roots
chapters.objective: Find all nth roots; prove the nth roots of unity sum to zero.
chapters.toughest: Roots-of-unity filters for binomial sums; cyclotomic polynomials and their irreducibility over Q.
chapters.proofs: Geometric-series proof of the zero sum.
chapters.quantum: Used again in the quantum Fourier transform (C069).

chapters.title: The Exponential Series
chapters.objective: Bridge: define exp by its power series and prove absolute convergence.
chapters.toughest: Convergence, rearrangement and the Cauchy product for complex series.

chapters.title: Euler's Formula, Derived Rigorously
chapters.objective: Derive e^(it) = cos t + i sin t from the series definitions; prove exp(z + w) = exp(z) exp(w).
chapters.toughest: The exponential as the unique continuous homomorphism from (R, +) onto the circle group with derivative i at 0; the Lie-group view of rotations.
chapters.proofs: Complete derivation; second proof via the differential equation f' = i f with uniqueness.
chapters.lab: Interactive rotation model: e^(it) traced on the unit circle with live checks of |e^(it)| = 1.

chapters.title: Computing with r e^(it)
chapters.objective: Multiply, divide and take powers in exponential form; meet e^(i pi) + 1 = 0.
chapters.toughest: JEE Advanced and olympiad problems in exponential form: products of sines, sums of cosines, polygon problems.

chapters.title: The Complex Logarithm and Complex Powers
chapters.objective: Define log z and z^w; understand why they are multivalued.
chapters.toughest: Branches of log and z^w; identities that fail and why; evaluating i^i and similar quantities exactly.
chapters.proofs: Counterexample: log(zw) = log z + log w fails for principal values.

chapters.title: Functions as Maps of the Plane
chapters.objective: Visualise w = z^2, 1/z and e^z as transformations.
chapters.toughest: Describe images of lines, circles and regions under standard maps exactly.
chapters.lab: Domain-colouring and grid-mapping explorer with a text description fallback.

chapters.title: Limits and Continuity in C
chapters.objective: Use epsilon-delta limits in the plane.
chapters.toughest: Epsilon-delta proofs for limits in the plane; continuity of branches and where it fails.

chapters.title: Complex Differentiability
chapters.objective: Define the complex derivative; prove conj(z) is nowhere complex-differentiable.
chapters.toughest: Decide complex differentiability of functions defined by formulas in x, y, z and conj(z).

chapters.title: The Cauchy–Riemann Equations
chapters.objective: Derive the Cauchy–Riemann equations; state the sufficient condition with exact hypotheses.
chapters.toughest: Cauchy–Riemann with minimal hypotheses (Looman–Menchoff stated); counterexamples at a point.
chapters.proofs: Necessity proof; sufficiency with continuous partials.

chapters.title: Holomorphic Functions
chapters.objective: Define holomorphic and entire functions on open sets, with first examples and non-examples.
chapters.toughest: Qualifying-exam problems on holomorphic functions: rigidity, closure properties, open mapping.

chapters.title: Harmonic Functions and Conjugates
chapters.objective: Show real and imaginary parts of holomorphic functions are harmonic; find harmonic conjugates.
chapters.toughest: Harmonic conjugates on non-simply-connected domains; mean-value property and the Dirichlet problem on a disc.
chapters.proofs: Proof assuming C^2 regularity (justified later by C044).

chapters.title: Power Series and the Radius of Convergence
chapters.objective: Find radii of convergence; state and prove the Cauchy–Hadamard formula.
chapters.toughest: Radii of convergence for hard series; behaviour on the boundary circle.

chapters.title: Power Series Are Holomorphic
chapters.objective: Prove power series can be differentiated term by term inside their disc.
chapters.toughest: Term-by-term differentiation proofs; zeros of power series and uniqueness.

chapters.title: Exponential and Trigonometric Functions in C
chapters.objective: Study exp, sin, cos, sinh and cosh on C: periods, zeros and unboundedness.
chapters.toughest: Zeros, periods and growth of exp, sin and cos; solving equations such as sin z = 2.
chapters.proofs: Proofs of periodicity and zero sets.

chapters.title: Conformal Maps and Möbius Transformations
chapters.objective: Show holomorphic maps preserve angles where f' is nonzero; study Möbius maps.
chapters.toughest: Find conformal maps between given regions; automorphisms of the disc and the upper half-plane.
chapters.proofs: Angle preservation proof; Möbius maps send circles and lines to circles and lines.

chapters.title: Paths and Contour Integrals
chapters.objective: Define integrals of complex functions along parametrised curves.
chapters.toughest: Contour integrals along standard and piecewise paths.

chapters.title: The ML Estimate
chapters.objective: Bound contour integrals by length times maximum.
chapters.toughest: Estimate integrals sharply enough to make them vanish in the limit.

chapters.title: Antiderivatives and Path Independence
chapters.objective: Use antiderivatives to evaluate contour integrals; see why 1/z has none on C minus 0.
chapters.toughest: Existence of antiderivatives and logarithms on given domains.
chapters.proofs: Fundamental theorem for contour integrals; integral of 1/z round the unit circle is 2 pi i.

chapters.title: Cauchy's Theorem
chapters.objective: State Cauchy's theorem with exact hypotheses and prove it via Goursat's theorem.
chapters.toughest: Qualifying-exam problems built on Cauchy's theorem; homotopy and homology versions with hypotheses.
chapters.proofs: Goursat for triangles; star-shaped domains in full; general version scoped with exact missing steps.

chapters.title: Cauchy's Integral Formula
chapters.objective: Prove the integral formula and the formula for derivatives.
chapters.toughest: Cauchy estimates and qualifying-exam problems on derivatives of holomorphic functions.

chapters.title: Holomorphic Implies Analytic
chapters.objective: Prove every holomorphic function has a convergent Taylor series locally.
chapters.toughest: Taylor expansions and radii from singularities; analyticity arguments in proofs.

chapters.title: Liouville's Theorem and a Proof of the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
chapters.objective: Prove Liouville's theorem and use it to prove the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra.
chapters.toughest: Liouville-type qualifying problems (entire functions with growth bounds are polynomials).

chapters.title: Maximum Modulus and the Identity Theorem
chapters.objective: Prove the maximum modulus principle and the identity theorem.
chapters.toughest: Maximum modulus, Schwarz's lemma and identity-theorem problems at qualifying level.

chapters.title: Morera's Theorem and Uniform Limits
chapters.objective: Prove Morera's theorem; show uniform limits of holomorphic functions are holomorphic.
chapters.toughest: Morera and Weierstrass convergence in qualifying problems; Hurwitz's theorem.

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: Laurent Series
chapters.objective: Expand functions in annuli; prove uniqueness of Laurent coefficients.
chapters.toughest: Laurent expansions in several annuli; coefficient formulas and uniqueness.

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: Isolated Singularities
chapters.objective: Classify removable singularities, poles and essential singularities.
chapters.toughest: Classify singularities, including at infinity; Casorati–Weierstrass and Picard (stated).

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: Residues and the Residue Theorem
chapters.objective: Prove the residue theorem for finitely many isolated singularities.
chapters.toughest: Residue-theorem problems at qualifying level.

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: Computing Residues
chapters.objective: Use practical rules for simple and higher-order poles.
chapters.toughest: Residues at higher-order poles and at infinity, quickly and correctly.

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: Real Integrals by Residues I
chapters.objective: Evaluate rational and trigonometric integrals with residues.
chapters.toughest: Hard rational and trigonometric integrals by residues.

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: Real Integrals by Residues II: Jordan's Lemma
chapters.objective: Evaluate Fourier-type integrals using Jordan's lemma.
chapters.toughest: Fourier-type and indented-contour integrals; principal values.
chapters.quantum: Fourier transform of a Lorentzian line shape.

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: The Argument Principle and Rouché's Theorem
chapters.objective: Count zeros and poles with contour integrals.
chapters.toughest: Count zeros in regions with Rouché; qualifying-exam root-counting problems.

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: Analytic Continuation
chapters.objective: Extend functions beyond their first domain; uniqueness from the identity theorem.
chapters.toughest: Continue functions defined by series and integrals; natural boundaries.

chapters.group_name: Laurent series, residues and analytic continuation
chapters.title: Branch Points and Branch Cuts
chapters.objective: Handle log and roots with explicit branch cuts.
chapters.toughest: Integrals and identities across branch cuts (keyhole contours).
chapters.proofs: Continuity of a chosen branch on the cut plane.

chapters.title: The Riemann Sphere
chapters.objective: Add a point at infinity via stereographic projection; Möbius maps as automorphisms.
chapters.toughest: Möbius maps as rotations of the sphere; cross-ratio problems.

chapters.title: Riemann Surfaces of sqrt(z) and log z
chapters.objective: Build the surfaces on which sqrt(z) and log z become single-valued.
chapters.toughest: Riemann surfaces of algebraic functions; genus by Riemann–Hurwitz (stated).
chapters.proofs: Constructions with precise gluing; topology prerequisites declared.

chapters.title: The Riemann Mapping Theorem
chapters.objective: State the theorem with exact hypotheses and understand its meaning.
chapters.toughest: Normal-families arguments and the proof structure of the Riemann mapping theorem.
chapters.proofs: Proof sketch with each missing step named.

chapters.title: Infinite Products and the Gamma Function
chapters.objective: Define Gamma by products and continuation; prove the reflection formula.
chapters.toughest: Gamma-function identities: reflection, duplication, Stirling's formula (proved).

chapters.title: The Riemann Zeta Function
chapters.objective: Continue zeta(s) and state the Riemann hypothesis precisely as an open problem.
chapters.toughest: Continuation and functional equation of zeta; trivial zeros; the Riemann hypothesis stated precisely as open.
chapters.proofs: Continuation sketch; open problem stated with a verified source.

chapters.title: Dispersion Relations and Causality
chapters.objective: Derive Kramers–Kronig relations with their hypotheses.
chapters.toughest: Derive Kramers–Kronig relations and apply them to a response function.
chapters.proofs: Derivation with stated decay and analyticity assumptions.
chapters.quantum: Response functions in physics; causality to analyticity.

chapters.title: Amplitudes: Complex Numbers That Give Probabilities
chapters.objective: Use the Born rule for a qubit with complex amplitudes; normalise a state.
chapters.toughest: Normalise states and compute measurement probabilities for complex amplitudes, including in rotated bases.

chapters.title: Global Phase and Relative Phase
chapters.objective: Prove a global phase changes no measurement probability; show a relative phase can.
chapters.toughest: Prove global phase is unobservable for every measurement; construct states differing only in relative phase.
chapters.proofs: Proof for any measurement basis; counterexample: |+> and |-> have equal standard-basis probabilities but differ in the X basis.
chapters.lab: Phase dial: global vs relative phase with live probabilities.

chapters.title: Interference: Add Amplitudes, Not Probabilities
chapters.objective: Derive |a + b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2 + 2 Re(a conj(b)) and read it as interference.
chapters.toughest: Multi-path interference sums and their probabilities.

chapters.title: The Mach–Zehnder Interferometer
chapters.objective: Model beam splitters and phase shifters as 2x2 complex matrices; derive cos^2 and sin^2 output probabilities.
chapters.toughest: Full Mach–Zehnder analysis with unbalanced splitters and losses.
chapters.lab: Interferometer lab with phase slider, probabilities and simulated counts; test oracle P0 + P1 = 1.

chapters.title: Phase on the Bloch Sphere
chapters.objective: See why the relative phase phi is a longitude on the Bloch sphere.
chapters.toughest: Map between amplitudes and Bloch angles; rotations as SU(2) acting on states.
chapters.proofs: Derivation of the Bloch parametrisation; global phase removed.

chapters.title: Phase Kickback and the Hadamard Test
chapters.objective: Estimate Re<psi|U|psi> from measurement probabilities.
chapters.toughest: Hadamard test and phase-estimation analysis with error bounds.

chapters.title: Roots of Unity in the Quantum Fourier Transform
chapters.objective: Build the DFT matrix and prove its columns are orthonormal.
chapters.toughest: Prove the QFT is unitary; analyse its action on periodic states.
chapters.proofs: Orthogonality proof from the roots-of-unity sum.

chapters.title: Unitary Evolution as Rotation
chapters.objective: Understand e^(-iEt/hbar) phases on energy eigenstates and the beats they create.
chapters.toughest: Time evolution of superpositions; beat frequencies; revival times.
chapters.quantum: Time evolution; relative phases between energy levels.

chapters.title: Reading a Complex Analysis Proof
chapters.objective: Read a full proof closely: hypotheses, quantifiers and each implication.
chapters.toughest: Reconstruct a classical proof unaided and find the step each hypothesis is used.
chapters.proofs: Guided reconstruction of a classical proof.

chapters.title: Complex Numbers in Software
chapters.objective: Handle floating point, atan2, branch cuts and cancellation in code.
chapters.toughest: Write numerically stable complex code: branch cuts, atan2, cancellation, tested to tolerance.

chapters.title: Research Ladder: Complex Analysis in Quantum Science
chapters.objective: Follow verified references from classical results to current research directions.
chapters.toughest: Read a current research paper's complex-analytic argument and state its assumptions.
chapters.proofs: Research ladder; only independently verified sources.

chapters.title: Capstone I: An Interference Experiment End to End
chapters.objective: Simulate an interferometer, compare counts with theory and report uncertainty.
chapters.toughest: Design, simulate and statistically test an interference experiment.

chapters.title: Capstone II: Prove and Present
chapters.objective: Write and present a complete proof of a major theorem from this domain.
chapters.toughest: Write and defend a complete proof of a major theorem from this domain.
chapters.proofs: Student-written proof assessed with a rubric.
